samples.summary: Row-selection and whole-sheet ('all') branches of the new `unsetRangeStyleKeys` are never exercised by any test
samples.evidence: The new suite only covers cell (`selectStart`), multi-cell (`selectStart`+`selectEnd`) and column (`selectColumn(1)`) selections. Nothing calls `selectRow(...)` or `selectAll()/selectAllCells()`, so `sheet.ts:4256-4265` (row-style conflict check), `4300-4311` (row-style rewrite) and `4281-4287` (`ownsSheet && this.sheetStyle` rewrite) plus the `!ownsSheet && this.sheetStyle?.[key]` bail at `4243` are entirely uncovered — roughly half the branch surface of the new method. A regression in the row or sheet layer (e.g. writing the wrong key set, or clearing a row style the selection does not own) would keep the suite green.
searchedFor: Grep for changeDecimals/unsetRangeStyleKeys across repo (only decimals.test.ts)

samples.summary: The range-patch ownership conflict path (`return false` when an overlapping patch is not fully contained in the selection) has no test
samples.evidence: `unsetRangeStyleKeys` refuses to write when a `rangeStyles` patch that sets one of the keys intersects the selection but is not contained by it (sheet.ts:4266-4276), and `changeDecimals` then falls back to an explicit `setRangeStyle`. The only conflict scenario tested is a *column* style ('should write an explicit value when a column style sets decimals', decimals.test.ts:162). No test creates, e.g., a dp patch on A1:C3 and then decreases decimals on A1 only, so both `rangesIntersect(...) && !owned(...)` and the corresponding `owned(patch.range)` shrink/split behaviour at 4315-4327 are only covered in the trivially-fully-owned case.

samples.summary: Non-inheritable number formats (currency, percent, date…) are untested for both `changeDecimals` and the `dp: 2` fallback in `getActiveDecimalState`
samples.evidence: `changeDecimals` gates restoration on `inheritable = !nf || nf === 'plain' || nf === 'number'` (sheet.ts:4202) and `getActiveDecimalState` returns a hard-coded `dp: 2` for any other format (sheet.ts:4185). No test in decimals.test.ts sets `nf: 'currency'`/`'percent'`; every test uses undefined/'plain'/'number'. So the branch that must keep an explicit `dp` (rather than restore inheritance) for a currency cell, and the `dp: 2` seed for such cells, are uncovered.

samples.summary: `removeCellStyleKeysInRange`'s merged-cell anchor normalization / `visited` de-duplication is untested
samples.evidence: The helper maps every grid ref through `normalizeRefToAnchor` and skips already-visited anchors (sheet.ts:4348-4355), specifically for merged cells. No test in decimals.test.ts creates a merge before calling `changeDecimals`, so if the anchor mapping or the dedup broke (e.g. deleting the wrong anchor cell of a merge) nothing would fail.

samples.summary: `decimalsInValue` has no direct unit test; its documented "0 for … text" contract is unverified and appears not to hold
samples.evidence: No test imports `decimalsInValue` (grep over packages/sheets/test returns only `formatValue` imports; test/model/format.test.ts covers formatValue only). Its doc comment claims `0` for text, but the implementation just looks for a '.', so a text value such as `abc.defg` yields 4, which would seed `valueDp` in `getActiveDecimalState`. The new suite only feeds numeric values ('12', '12.5', '12.34', '1234.5'), so this claimed case is untested.

samples.summary: 'should keep a number format the user chose' cannot detect a wrong stored `dp` — its display assertion passes whether `dp: 2` is stored or removed
samples.evidence: After `changeDecimals(-1)` the test only asserts `nf === 'number'` and that the display equals `formatValue('12', 'number', 2)`. Since `nf: 'number'` renders 2 decimals when no `dp` is stored, the display assertion holds both when the intended explicit `dp: 2` is written and when `dp` is dropped entirely — exactly the distinction the new `DefaultStyleValues`/`explicitDp` work exists to preserve. An explicit `expect(await sheet.getStyle(...)).toEqual({ dp: 2, nf: 'number' })` would pin it.

samples.summary: Expected display strings are computed with the production `formatValue`, weakening the assertions
samples.evidence: Lines 31-33 and 157-159 compare `toDisplayString(...)` against `formatValue('12', 'number', 1|2)` instead of literals ('12.0', '12.00'). Any shared bug in `formatValue` cancels out on both sides; literal expectations would make the assertion independent of the code path under test.

searchedFor: Grep for changeDecimals/unsetRangeStyleKeys across repo (only decimals.test.ts)

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `unsetRangeStyleKeys` (sheet.ts:4231-4341) branches on `selectionType === 'all'` / `'row'` to derive `ownsSheet`/`ownsRows` (4236-4238), gating the sheet-style bail (4243), the row conflict scan (4256-4265), the sheet-style rewrite (4281-4287) and the row-style rewrite (4300-4311). Its only caller is `changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4208), which in turn is only invoked from spreadsheet.ts:536/546 and from decimals.test.ts. Reading decimals.test.ts in full, every test sets the selection via `selectStart` (cell), `selectStart`+`selectEnd` (multi-cell), or `selectColumn(1)` (lines 165, 184) — never `selectRow(...)` or `selectAll()/selectAllCells()`, both of which exist and are used in formatting.test.ts:192,525,536,556. Repo-wide greps for `changeDecimals`, `unsetRangeStyleKeys`, `increaseDecimals|decreaseDecimals`, `[Dd]ecimal` in test/spec files, and `omitStyleKeys` in the test tree turn up no other exercise of these paths (the frontend toolbar caller at formatting-toolbar.tsx:249,253 has no test). So the row-layer and whole-sheet-layer behavior of a new public method — including the "bail out rather than mask an unownable inherited value" rule for sheet and row styles — ships with no test that could fail if it regressed. That is a clear behavior surface with no meaningful coverage, which is major under the missing-tests limb of this lens; the tested cell/range/column layers are separate code paths, so they would not catch a row/sheet-layer regression.

The only conflict scenario tested is a *column* style ('should write an explicit value when a column style sets decimals', decimals.test.ts:162). No test creates, e.g., a dp patch on A1:C3 and then decreases decimals on A1 only, so both `rangesIntersect(...) && !owned(...)` and the corresponding `owned(patch.range)` shrink/split behaviour at 4315-4327 are only covered in the trivially-fully-owned case.

verdict.reason: The range-patch conflict branch of `unsetRangeStyleKeys` (sheet.ts:4266-4276, `rangesIntersect(t, patch.range) && !owned(patch.range)` -> return false) is unreachable from any existing test. `unsetRangeStyleKeys` is called only from `changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4208); `changeDecimals` is called only from spreadsheet.ts:534/544 (untested, driven only from formatting-toolbar.tsx) and from decimals.test.ts. In decimals.test.ts the only rangeStyles patches created are single-cell (lines 145, 210) or the A1:B2 patch at line 110 that is unset with the identical A1:B2 selection - the trivially fully-owned case hitting the delete branch at 4324-4326. I re-checked the reviewer's key premise myself: the 'column style sets decimals' test (decimals.test.ts:162-179) does NOT create a rangeStyles patch, because setRangeStyle short-circuits for selectionType === 'column' into colStyles/store.setColumnStyle and returns early (sheet.ts:3698-3709); it therefore covers the colStyles conflict branch (4246-4255), which is separate logic. No test makes a patch overlap the selection only partially, so neither the `return false` conflict nor the 'not owned -> keep patch intact' path at 4319-4321 is exercised. A newly added public method whose documented conflict rule ships with zero coverage on its range-patch layer is a real missing-test defect (major) under this lens.
